clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8106 is its operative paragraph, which exempts Frank B. Bourn from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that Frank B. Bourn, who "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1939, by Executive Order No. 7863 of April 7, 1938", be further exempted; the order is a further exemption of an employee already exempted by earlier orders, which are separate instruments. The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on June 30, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. EO 8420 (dated May 28, 1940 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1941"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period.

research_rationale:
EO 8106 (May 3, 1939) exempts Frank B. Bourn from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending June 30, 1940", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on June 30, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. Later extension orders are recorded as later events and do not end this order's clause. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
